text:
maria: Heads up — p95 decode latency spiked on canary after today's merge (release/4983). Short seqs (<=8 tokens) are ~2.4x slower. Saw it around 12:07 UTC in the perf dashboard :eyes:
ajay: Yup. Canary link: https://perf/redwood/release/4983 — shortseq p95 96ms -> 233ms. Tagged the run with decode-path and shortseq.
tomas: I grabbed a full trace (trace-id ab12f3). The decode path shows the fused-attn branch doing an extra memcpy during prefetch/kv handling. Looks correlated with commit 0f9a3b (batcher/prefetch scheduling tweak).
jen: Quick flame sample pasted below:
```
CPU%  Function
48    decode_loop
30    fused_attn_kernel
12    kv_prefetch
8     memcpy
```
memcpy jumps when shortseq workload runs.
maria: That matches what I was thinking — the batching change lowered microbatch coalescing so we now prefetch per microbatch more often. More prefetches -> more memcpy -> higher tail.
perf-bot: alert: CANARY_LATENCY_REGRESSION detected (release 4983). metric: p95_shortseq baseline=96ms current=233ms delta=+143ms.
ajay: Ran a quick bisect. Reverting 0f9a3b brings p95 back to ~110ms on the canary pool. Revert looks promising.
tomas: Confirmed locally too. Also observed kv_evictions/sec spike: 0.02 -> 2.1. Looks like prefetch floods KV and causes maintenance to evict hot entries, amplifying misses.
jen: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- revert 0f9a3b in canary (fast)
- add coalescing: don't prefetch for keys already touched by earlier microbatch in the same request
- cheap shortseq check: skip prefetch for <=8 token paths unless we predict benefit
I'll sketch patches for the coalescing logic.
maria: Can someone open the revert PR and tag it for canary rollback? If revert goes in, we should still follow up with the coalescing change.
ajay: On it — opening PR 7342 with the revert + an integration perf test that runs synthetic shortseq with KV churn.
tomas: I'll add a CI perf job for the <=8 token synthetic to catch regressions like this in the future.
jen: Note for postmortem: rollout criteria missed shortseq heavy workloads. Add a targeted checklist to run shortseq+kv churn perf tests before large batching/prefetch changes.
maria: Thanks everyone. tagging oncall for rollback scheduling. @sre-bot can you schedule a canary rollback window? :pray:
sre-bot: Incident: scheduled canary rollback window 18:00 UTC. Infra notified and will stand by.
